correctness.rationale: From the exact n-dependent urn transition and absorbing-killed first moment, A_(n+1)=A_n+u_n. Since up-step probabilities are at most 1/2 at positive positions, a monotone coupling to simple symmetric random walk gives u_(2n) ≤ 2A_n/(n sqrt(n+1)). Monotonicity bounds u_j by summable coefficients times A_floor(j/2), and finite-tail absorption establishes sup A_n<∞, hence u_n=O(n^-3/2) and finite mean. Independent exact-rational finite checks reproduce the recurrence through eighty steps.

originality.rationale: The full HTML source of Balaji and Mahmoud (arXiv:2504.14813, Sections 4–5) labels finite mean first return as an open conjecture and only reports simulation; their Eulerian-number marginals do not imply it. The argument uses a previously unstated killed-first-moment recurrence and an SRW survival coupling to give a quantitative n^-3/2 bound. Bertoin (arXiv:2105.09569) analyzes standard elephant-walk zero returns, with p=0 deterministic first return under his initialization; that is not the Friedman initial boundary problem. Priority risk remains if an unstated general level-hitting theorem subsumes this proof.
residual_risks: General historical theorem for first passage to a nonzero level of an anti-persistent elephant walk with deterministic additional initial steps could imply the bound, despite no such statement found in inspected sources.
The O(n^-3/2) upper bound need not be the exact tail order; no lower bound asserted.

value.rationale: Balaji and Mahmoud explicitly pose the finite-mean-first-return question as a new conjecture after a simulation. Establishing a finite mean with quantitative survival decay is a naturally motivated first-passage theorem for their opposite-reinforcing urn walk, and the exact killed-first-moment/coupling mechanism is structural rather than an arbitrary finite census.
